_nota: Summary of the INIFAP 2026 Agricultural Technical Agenda, made from the text in data/inifap/extraido/michoacan.json following pipeline/inifap/instrucciones_resumen.md. No pesticide brands or doses.
fuente: INIFAP. Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Michoacán [Agricultural Technical Agenda of Michoacán]. INIFAP, Mexico City, 2026.

fichas.region: Semi-warm and temperate subhumid climates (ACw and Cw) between 1,200 and 2,400 m a.s.l. (optimum 1,500–2,200), 17–24 °C, 800–2,000 mm of rain from May to October; sandy loam soils of volcanic ash (andosols, "tupuri") and slopes no greater than 25 %. In ACw climates it may require irrigation from December to May.

siembra.texto: Without irrigation: at the onset of the rainy season, planting the pit of a landrace (local variety) avocado and grafting it the following year. With irrigation or a good rainy season: plant the already grafted tree with its root ball, with about 2 kg of compost at the bottom of the planting hole.

fichas.densidad: Square layout. Low: 12 x 12, 10 x 10 or 8 x 8 m; medium: 7 x 7, 7 x 6 or 7 x 5 m; high: 7 x 4, 5 x 5 or 3 x 3 m (on raised beds, with fertigation and intensive pruning).
fichas.fertilizacion: Each ton of fruit removes 3.5 kg of N, 1.5 of P and 4.5 of K: apply at least 35-15-45 kg of N-P-K for every 10 t harvested, highly split because the soil leaches the nutrients. With irrigation: 10–15 kg/ha per week of N-P2O5-K2O + micronutrients and calcium nitrate separately (or, optionally, 30 kg/ha per month + 10 kg/ha of calcium nitrate). Rainfed: 100 kg/ha of the blend + 20 kg/ha of calcium nitrate at the beginning, middle and end of the rains. Well-fermented compost: 10–20 kg per plant at the onset of the rains.
fichas.riego: Drip on loam or sandy loam soils; micro-sprinklers on sandy soils. Irrigate from December to May, until the first rains: with drip, 1 hour twice a week from December to February and three times a week from March. If water is short, do not go below 50 % of the recommended amount.
plagas: Leafroller, leafminer and other defoliating caterpillars
fichas.malezas: The agenda asks not to use herbicides: keep weeds short, without pulling them out, and leave them on the soil as mulch or use them for compost; use a hand-held or tractor brush cutter. During avocado flowering, let the weeds flower to attract pollinators and cut them afterwards. Where allowed, restricted grazing.
fichas.cosecha: Maturity when the skin turns from bright light green to dark green (Hass); from flower to mature fruit about 10 months elapse between 1,600 and 2,000 m a.s.l. Cut with clean shears leaving 0.5–1 cm of stem, into padded containers and without exposure to the sun. Store at 5–7 °C (2–4 °C if already ripe) with 85–95 % relative humidity. Yield: about 15 t/ha in a good rainy season and temperate climate.
cuidados: Sample thrips by tapping the flowers over a white piece of cardboard: with more than 10 insects, start control.
Every year prune the branches without fruit and, after harvest, those that already produced, to control height and let in light and air.
Cut and burn branches with borers; bury damaged fruit 1.5 m deep (or burn it).
Make a tree basin and leave the leaf litter as mulch on young trees and on slopes of more than 5 %.
Split fertilization into small, frequent doses to prevent leaching.
Against anthracnose and scab: cut fruit with the first lesions and prune inner branches for ventilation.
fichas.nota: Table 3 (cost-benefit) does not appear in the extracted text; the extract only had a B/C ratio of 1.2 and a yield of 1.0 that could not be confirmed, so no costs were copied.

fichas.region: Semi-arid warm tropics of Tierra Caliente (La Huacana, Huetamo, Churumuco, Apatzingán, etc.), from 0 to 600 m a.s.l., 500–1,100 mm of rain and 25–27 °C; medium-depth soils, sandy or clayey loam, pH 7.5–8.5.

siembra.texto: DDR Apatzingán and La Huacana: July 1 to 15. Huetamo: once the rainy season has set in and up to July 5. Plant into moist soil at 2 cm depth.

fichas.densidad: 6 kg/ha of certified seed. Apatzingán and La Huacana: rows 70 cm apart, drilled at mid-slope of the furrow, 5–10 cm between plants. Huetamo (ox team): rows 60 cm apart, hills of 20–30 seeds every 50 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Apatzingán and La Huacana: 30-20-00 at planting, drilled below and to one side of the seed and covered (e.g. 65 kg of urea and 43 kg of triple superphosphate). Huetamo: 60-40-00 at planting or at the first cultivation (e.g. 130 kg of urea and 67 kg of triple superphosphate).
fichas.riego: If water is available, irrigate at planting, at the start of flowering and at fruit set.
fichas.malezas: Keep the crop clean for the first 30 days. Make 1 or 2 cultivator passes (2 cultivations in Huetamo): the first weeding within 15 days after emergence and the second 15–20 days later. Common weeds: quelite, foxtail, bejuco, zacate pitillo, meloncillo, mancacoyote, picha, pindinicua and pastora.
fichas.cosecha: Cut between 90 and 105 days after sowing, when the leaves drop and the plant turns yellowish. Make bundles of 15–18 cm, form shocks of 10–12 bundles, let them dry 15–20 days and thresh. Deliver the grain without stems or capsules. Expected yield with irrigation: 1,000 kg/ha.
cuidados: Plow deeper than 25 cm and leave the land free of clods: the seed is small.
On rolling hills, furrow on the contour following the contour lines.
If there was a lot of stem rot, do not plant sesame, sorghum or melon on that land for the next two years.
Avoid excess moisture, rotate crops and burn residues to prevent root rot.
Check for stink bugs from flowering and cutworms from emergence: the agenda gives thresholds (25 stink bugs per 100 net sweeps; 2 cut plants per meter).
Cut on time and deliver clean grain so the price is not docked.
fichas.nota: The header says irrigated regime and the cost table includes irrigations, but planting dates depend on the onset of the rains. Costs confirmed with Table 6 (gross income 26,000).

fichas.region: ACw and Cw2 climates between 1,200 and 2,000 m a.s.l. (Bajío of Michoacán, Zamora, Los Reyes, Tangancícuaro, Pátzcuaro, Ziracuaretiro), 16–22 °C, cool winters; sandy or loam volcanic ash soils, or in pots with substrate; slope less than 5 %.

siembra.texto: Transplant the nursery plant at 20–30 cm tall and with several branches, into the soil (10 x 10 x 10 cm hole with pine compost and coconut fiber) or into 25–30 L containers with substrate at pH 5–5.5. The agenda does not give a planting date.

fichas.densidad: Single row: 40–60 cm between plants and 1.8–2.0 m between rows. Other options: low (3 x 3 or 4 x 2 m), medium (1.5 x 1.5 m, backyard) and high (0.5 m between plants and 1.5 m between rows).
fichas.fertilizacion: Macro- and micronutrients to the soil three times a week from transplanting to the first harvest (e.g. triple 19 at 50 g in 20 L of water, humic acids and phosphoric acid), plus a foliar biostimulant every 14 days. Keep the pH between 5.8 and 6.0 with phosphoric acid (2 mL in 20 L of water).
fichas.riego: Drip all year round, even in the rainy season (in open field at least every 3–4 days). One 2–4 L/h emitter per plant; 10 minutes per irrigation, 2 to 4 times a day, and every day in the dry season.
fichas.malezas: Weekly hand weeding inside the pots and brush cutter every month on paths and surroundings to eliminate pest hosts.
fichas.cosecha: Harvest is entirely manual. From transplanting or pruning to sprouting 4–6 months elapse, and from flowering to the end of harvest another 4–6; the cycle repeats every year. Average state yield of 10–15 t/ha (potential of 40 t/ha).
cuidados: Check the substrate pH often, especially at flowering, and correct it if it goes above 6.
Irrigate frequently all year round: blueberry does not tolerate the substrate drying out.
Biloxi needs cross-pollination (plant with another variety) and frost protection because of its early flowering.
Surround the stem with powdered sulfur against ants and control the leafroller with beneficial fungi.
Use bird netting at the ends of the high tunnels.
fichas.nota: Although the header says rainfed/irrigated, the agenda states that all plantings in Michoacán require drip irrigation. Costs from Table 9: gross income 1,200,000; the price per kg does not appear in the text (null).

fichas.region: Apatzingán Valley (Lombardía, Parácuaro, Tepalcatepec): warm semi-arid climate, 250–800 m a.s.l., 20–34 °C and 600–800 mm of rain from July to September; clayey, alkaline Vertisols (pH 7.5–8.5), poor in organic matter and nitrogen; slope less than 5 %.

siembra.texto: Spring-Summer: planting from June to July and harvest from October to November (the most productive cycle). Fall-Winter: planting in December and harvest from May to June; there is very little area because rice does not tolerate temperatures below 18 °C.

fichas.densidad: Dry planting with a seed drill: 80 kg/ha of seed, rows 20 cm apart (or broadcast). Wet broadcast planting: 70–80 kg/ha. Transplanting 20–30-day-old seedlings: 20–25 kg/ha of seed.
fichas.fertilizacion: Low-fertility soils: 0.5 t/ha of the 30-10-10 blend at planting or transplanting (or 20 days later) and, 45–60 days later, 0.2–0.3 t/ha of 33-0-0. More fertile soils: 250 kg of urea at each of those two times, with foliar applications. Biofertilizers (cyanobacteria, mycorrhizae) can be used at 1–2 L/ha.
fichas.riego: In the Valley, scheduled irrigation in border basins and rainfed with supplemental irrigation are used: keep the soil saturated in the vegetative phase and flooded (2.5–10 cm water depth) in the reproductive phase. Lack of water during grain filling greatly reduces yield.
fichas.malezas: Weeds are more of a problem in direct seeding than in transplanting. Prepare the land well in advance to "solarize" the soil and expose weed seeds; rotate with sugarcane; clean levees and ditches with a brush cutter; flood after transplanting if water is available. Selective chemical control for rice can be used.
fichas.cosecha: At 140–150 days after sowing, when the panicle is golden and dry. Check every 15 days: when the panicle releases the grain on squeezing, go in with the combine so as not to lose grain. Expected yield: 8–10 t/ha.
cuidados: Prepare the land very well (plowing to 30 cm, harrowing, land leveling and borders of 1.4–1.8 m): after planting, machinery can no longer enter.
Do not burn the residues of the previous crop if they have already been shredded; leave them on the soil.
Use clean, healthy and disinfected seed to prevent neck rot and other diseases.
Prefer varieties resistant to Pyricularia (Pacífico FL-15, Golfo FL-16).
Against the borer, remove crop residues and release Trichogramma.
Do not let water run short during the grain filling stage.
fichas.nota: The agenda header says "Perennial", but the text treats it as a SS or FW cycle crop (harvest at 140–150 days); it was set as annual. Cycle null because the entry covers SS and FW. In costs (Table 12), the yield of 6,857 kg/ha is consistent with the cost per kg (6.22) and gross income of 48,000; the price does not appear explicitly (null).

fichas.region: Tierra Caliente, Balsas Depression and Costa-Sierra (e.g. Nuevo Urecho, Taretan, Ziracuaretiro, Churumuco, Lázaro Cárdenas): warm subhumid climate, 0–800 m a.s.l., 24–28 °C, 1,500–2,500 mm of rain and 70–90 % relative humidity; loam, deep and well-drained soils, pH 5.5–7.0, slope less than 15 %. It needs shade.

siembra.texto: Plant at the onset of the rains, from June to August, with nursery plants in 40 x 40 x 30 cm planting holes with organic matter, the rootstock facing east and the graft facing west. Establish temporary shade (banana, maize or cassava) and permanent shade (cedar, mahogany, huanacaxtle, gliricidia, mango).

fichas.densidad: Most common: 3 x 3 m (1,111 plants/ha) in a shaded agroforestry system. Other options from 2 x 2 m (2,500 plants/ha) to 5 x 5 m (400 plants/ha).
fichas.fertilizacion: Do soil and foliar analyses before fertilizing. Establishment (6–12 months): 50–100 g per plant of 20-10-6-5 (N-P-K-S) and 1–2 kg of compost. Young plants (under 5 years): mainly N and P, 2–3 times a year. Medium production (5–10 years): 0.8–1.0 kg per plant of NPK with micronutrients and 2–4 kg of humus or chicken manure, 2 times a year. Full production (over 10 years): 1.0–1.2 kg per plant of 16-8-24 and 5–10 kg of organic fertilizers, 2–3 times a year.
fichas.riego: Drip every 4–7 days depending on the soil, or furrow (gravity) irrigation every 15–30 days during the dry season where there are canals.
fichas.malezas: Brush clearing with a machete at ground level, cover crops, mulch with organic residues and good shade management to reduce weeds.
fichas.cosecha: Pods ripen 4–5 months after pollination: they change from green to yellow or from red to orange. Cut with a sharp tool without damaging the flower cushions; ferment 3–4 days (criollo types) to 6–8 days (forastero types) and dry the beans to 6–8 % moisture. Store in sacks on pallets, with relative humidity below 80 %. Potential in Michoacán: 700–900 kg/ha of dry beans; it produces from 3–5 years of age.
cuidados: Provide shade from the start (70 % in the first years) and then adjust it to about 60 % light and 40 % shade.
Do formative, maintenance and sanitary pruning, and remove suckers; disinfect tools so as not to spread Ceratocystis wilt (mal de machete).
Remove diseased pods on time to slow frosty pod rot and black pod.
Use clones tolerant to frosty pod rot such as those validated by INIFAP.
When controlling pests, protect the cocoa pollinating midge (Forcipomyia).
On hillsides, plant on contour lines.
fichas.nota: Table 18 (establishment cost-benefit) does not appear in the extracted text; the extract only had a B/C ratio of 1.3 and a yield of 1.0 that could not be confirmed. The text mentions a price of $130 per kg of dry beans (FIRA, 2026).

fichas.region: Sandy or sandy loam soils, deep, salt-free and well drained, with pH 6.0 to 6.5; 15–25 °C and 60–70 % relative humidity. It needs chill hours (below 7 °C) for good flowering and fruit set.

siembra.texto: Being perennial, it can produce all year round depending on the variety; the agenda does not give a planting date.

fichas.fertilizacion: Total of 200-100-180 kg/ha of N-P2O5-K2O split by stage: vegetative-flowering 45-60-20; flowering-start of fruiting 35-50-80; fruiting-harvest 120-0-80. Adjust with prior soil and foliar analysis.
fichas.riego: Irrigation every 4–7 days as needed, never letting moisture run short and avoiding waterlogging.
fichas.malezas: Solarize the soil and use plastic mulch; without mulch, hand (or chemical) weeding. Common weeds: nutsedge, morning glory, spurge (golondrina), mallow, bluegrass, quelite, clover and purslane.
fichas.cosecha: The first harvest comes 60 to 240 days after transplanting (130 on average) depending on the variety; then picking takes place every 2–30 days (3 on average) for 60–720 days. Yields of 13 to 78 t/ha per year depending on the variety (e.g. Frontera 31 t, San Andreas 78 t).
cuidados: Monitor every week walking in a zigzag and checking 60 leaflets; if there are 5 mites per leaflet, treat.
Against the first mite infestations, use low-impact products and release predatory mites.
Alternate miticides with different modes of action to avoid resistance.
Use raised beds, good drainage and crop rotation to prevent root diseases.
Remove dry leaves and weeds, which are sources of reinfection.
Do not apply pesticides when plants are stressed.
fichas.nota: Table 25: the printed net income (391,740) does not match gross income of 900,000 minus cost of 691,740 (= 208,260; the 30.1 % return does correspond to 208,260), so it was left as null. The table has no yield or price.

fichas.region: Eastern (DDR Zitácuaro) and central (DDR Uruapan) zones: semi-warm or temperate subhumid climate with summer rains, 600–1,900 m a.s.l. and 23–30 °C; deep soils, with organic matter and good drainage, optimum pH 6 to 7. It is grown rainfed or irrigated.

siembra.texto: Rainfed, at the onset of the rains; with irrigation, at any time of the year. Planting holes of 0.50 x 0.50 x 0.50 m with organic matter; rows running north to south.

fichas.densidad: Spacings of 4.5 x 1.5, 4 x 3, 4 x 4, 5 x 5 or 6 x 6 m, in line or staggered (triangular): from 277 to 1,480 plants per ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: At planting: 500 g of triple calcium superphosphate at the bottom of the planting hole (or 3–5 kg of dry manure). Young trees: 200 g of triple 16 per tree every 4 months the first year, 400 g the second and 600 g the third. In production: 220 g of 10-10-10 per 2.5 cm of trunk diameter per year, in the tree basin.
fichas.riego: Rainfed orchards are not irrigated. With irrigation (usually drip), calculate the water per tree according to evapotranspiration and tree age.
fichas.malezas: Manual control with scythe, hoe or brush cutter around the tree; mowing in producing orchards during the rains; harrowing only in young orchards, at the beginning and end of the rainy season, without harrowing under producing trees.
fichas.cosecha: From flowering to harvest 90–150 days elapse depending on the variety; the main harvest is in fall-winter, but with defoliation, pruning and irrigation it can be induced at other times. For processing, harvest with yellow skin; for fresh market or long transport, yellowish green. Harvest early and store cold (8–10 °C for yellowish-green fruit; 5–8 °C for ripe fruit; 90 % relative humidity).
cuidados: Against the guava fruit fly: bag the fruit, place McPhail traps and remove damaged fruit and weeds.
Against the weevil: bag until harvest and remove damaged fruit before the larva emerges.
Do production pruning after each harvest: the fruit grows on new shoots.
Use yellow traps and remove weeds and crop debris to check aphids.
Reduce humidity (bagging, aeration pruning) to prevent anthracnose and scab.
On sloping land, build contour lines.
fichas.nota: Costs from Table 28 (maintenance of trees over 11 years old): gross income 156,000. The value of 41,000 appears mislabeled as "gross income $ t-1", but it matches net income (156,000 − 114,960 = 41,040). The price per ton does not appear explicitly (null). Establishing the orchard costs 106,600 per ha (Table 27).

fichas.region: Dry tropics (La Huacana, Tzitzio, Aquila, Churumuco, Huetamo): warm subhumid or warm dry climate, 0–900 m a.s.l. (best 200 to 600), 25–30 °C and relative humidity below 70 %; well-drained sandy loam soils, pH 5.6–6.8. It does not tolerate waterlogging or frost.

siembra.texto: From June to July, at the onset of the rains. Direct seeding of 3 to 5 seeds per hill, with later thinning if needed.

fichas.densidad: 0.90 m between plants and 1.30 m between rows, or 1 x 1 m; 1–2 kg of seed per ha. With the INIFAP varieties, the high density of 13,889 plants/ha yielded more than the low density of 8,264 plants/ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: Best with soil analysis; 45-30-20 of N-P-K can be applied in two parts, at 20 and 45 days after sowing, and foliar fertilizer every 15 days in the first two months. Also crop stubble, legumes, green manures or cover crops (mucuna, canavalia).
fichas.malezas: Hand weeding with hoe, scythe or machete, one or more weedings during the cycle; one cultivator pass to hill up soil and clean the bottom of the furrow. Leave the pulled weeds as cover. Common weeds: lentejilla, mala mujer, quelite, chayotillo, abrojo, panguica, huizache and Johnson grass.
fichas.cosecha: When the plant naturally drops 90 % of its leaves and the seeds of the lower capsules turn from white to brown or black; in the region, from November 25 to December 30. Strip the calyces the same day as cutting and dry them in the sun 3–8 days, covering them at night, down to 12 % moisture. Average state yield of 670 kg/ha; with improved varieties, high density and topping, yields from 1,100 to more than 1,600 kg/ha have been obtained.
cuidados: Do topping (remove 10–15 cm of the terminal bud) at 90 days after sowing, before flowering.
Use seed from the previous harvest (no more than one year old) and select it from the plants with the largest calyces.
Plant red-stemmed varieties and ensure good drainage against stem rot.
Plant early to escape the whitefly, which arrives at the end of the cycle.
Do not harvest too early: it lowers yield and calyx quality.
Cover the calyces at night during drying so the dew does not wet them.
fichas.nota: The agenda header says "Perennial", but the text describes it as an annual plant sown in June-July; it was set as annual. Costs from Table 29 with the Estrella costeña variety and apical pruning.

fichas.region: Four regions: Bajío of Michoacán (1,700–2,300 m a.s.l., fertile Vertisols, the most productive); High Valleys (temperate climate, 900–1,200 mm of rain); Neovolcanic Axis and Meseta Purépecha (1,200–3,000 m a.s.l., light, low-fertility soils that fix phosphorus); and Apatzingán Valley and Coast (warm, 400–800 mm, allows SS and FW plantings).

siembra.texto: Bajío and High Valleys: full irrigation from March 15 to May 15; limited irrigation (one pre-planting irrigation, then rain) from May 1 to June 15. Meseta Purépecha by altitude: 2,400–2,600 m from March 10 to 25; 2,200–2,400 m from April 1 to 20; 2,000–2,200 m from April 20 to May 20. Apatzingán Valley (irrigated SS): from May 15 to June 30; late plantings with early or intermediate hybrids up to July 30.

variedades: Native maize landraces in the Meseta Purépecha
fichas.densidad: Bajío and High Valleys: 75,000 plants/ha (23–26 kg/ha of seed). Meseta Purépecha: 45,000–62,500 plants/ha (20–25 kg/ha). Apatzingán Valley: 75,000 plants/ha (18–20 kg/ha). Do a germination test and add 1 kg/ha of seed for every 10 seeds that do not emerge.
fichas.fertilizacion: Bajío and High Valleys (full irrigation): 250-46-00; half the N and all the P at planting and the rest between the 8th and 10th leaf (or in three parts, the last at flag leaf). Meseta Purépecha: 120-90-00; at planting 200 kg of 18-46-00 and at the first cultivation, at 40–50 days, 130 kg of urea; biofertilizer on the seed (500–1,000 g/ha). Apatzingán Valley: 120-40-00; half the N and all the P at planting and the rest at the first cultivation, irrigating the next day. Foliar with micronutrients and seaweed extract at V4–V6 and V8–V10.
fichas.riego: Plant after irrigation, when the soil is at the right moisture ("a punto"). Under limited irrigation, planting is in May and then the rains take over; a second irrigation may be needed between July and August if it does not rain for two weeks. Avoid water shortage from flag leaf until pollen shed. Technified irrigation raises yield but also costs.
fichas.malezas: Critical period: the first 40 days after sowing. Cultural control with hoe or machete (only on small areas), mechanical with a cultivator (two cultivations: at 20–30 and 30–40 days) or chemical with pre-emergents in the first 3 days and post-emergents at 12–15 days.
fichas.cosecha: Bajío and High Valleys: at 13–15 % grain moisture, or at physiological maturity (black layer at the grain tip) if it is to be shocked. Meseta: in late fall and winter, by hand. Apatzingán: summer plantings from November to December and winter plantings until May, at 14–15 % moisture. Market at 12–14 % moisture. Yields: 5.3–8.2 t/ha in Bajío and High Valleys, 2–3 t/ha in the Meseta and 7–10 t/ha in Apatzingán.
cuidados: From 15–20 days after sowing, check for fall armyworm and continue monitoring throughout the cycle.
Place 3–5 pheromone traps per ha at planting and release Trichogramma wasps against fall armyworm and corn earworm.
Plant on the recommended dates: early or late plantings have more leafhoppers and corn stunt.
Keep the crop weed-free for the first 40 days.
Apply fertilizer covered with soil and with moisture in the soil, in two or three parts.
Store grain under a roof, off the ground; against the weevil, pine ash can be used (10 g per kg of maize every 3 months).
fichas.nota: Modality null because the entry covers rainfed and irrigated in several regions; the main cycle is SS, although in Apatzingán it is also planted in FW (no dates in the agenda). Costs from Table 30 (irrigated): gross income 48,000 = 10 t × 4,800 $/t. Hybrids from private companies (national and transnational) go in hibridos_comerciales.

fichas.region: Tierra Caliente and coast (Huetamo, La Huacana, San Lucas, Coahuayana, Churumuco, Apatzingán): tropics and subtropics, 0–500 m a.s.l., 22–25 °C and dry climate; soils deeper than 60 cm, light, sandy loam, with good drainage and pH 7–7.5. It is produced with fertigation and plastic mulch.

siembra.texto: Fall-Winter cycle, from December 1 to February 15. Hand planting of one seed every 25 cm, in moist soil after the first irrigation.

fichas.densidad: Borders 1.60 m apart with two-tone plastic mulch (silver/black) and one seed every 25 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Total 180-100-200 kg/ha of N-P-K. Before planting, after forming the borders, 90-100-100 (urea, triple superphosphate and potassium sulfate). Through fertigation: 22.5 kg of N at 25, 35, 45 and 65 days and 50 kg of K at 45 and 65 days (urea and potassium nitrate). Apply 3 L of phosphoric acid at each irrigation to keep the drip tape clean.
fichas.riego: First irrigation before planting, 12 hours with the fertigation system; afterwards, 8-hour irrigations every 7 days.
fichas.malezas: Black mulch prevents almost all weeds; hand weed the planting hole 5 days after the melon emerges. Outside the mulch, manual control or chemical control directed only at the weeds, without wetting the melon. Common weeds: quelite, nutsedge, goosegrass, purslane, chayotillo and Bermuda grass.
fichas.cosecha: Physiological maturity at 60–65 days after sowing, at about 12 °Brix; harvest by hand with ayates (carrying cloths). Expected yield with mulch and fertigation: 40 t/ha.
cuidados: Plow at least one month before planting, to 20–30 cm.
Use hybrids resistant or tolerant to Fusarium and powdery mildew.
Control aphids and whitefly, which transmit viruses.
Arrange the vines late in the day so as not to transmit viruses through handling.
Turn the fruit twice so the netting forms well and it does not rot in contact with moist soil.
Use light traps to catch adult white grubs.
fichas.nota: Table 33: the printed yield (320,000 kg/ha) is actually the gross income; 40 t/ha was used, which is the expected yield in the text and matches the cost of 3.826 $/kg. Net income appears as "166,944-9" (= 320,000 − 153,055.10). The price does not appear explicitly (null).

fichas.region: Tierra Caliente and coast of Michoacán, below 1,000 m a.s.l., 23–26 °C and 70–85 % relative humidity; deep, fertile, well-drained soils, sandy loam to loam, with pH 6.0–7.0 and slope less than 1 %. It needs 1,800–2,000 mm of water per year, so it is supplemented with irrigation.

siembra.texto: The best transplants are from March to May (greater growth and fewer virus-transmitting insects). With irrigation it can be transplanted all year round and, rainfed, at the onset of the rains. Transplant 30–45-day-old nursery seedlings with 4–6 leaves, without burying the collar.

fichas.densidad: 3.0 x 1.5 m (2,222 plants/ha), 2.0 x 2.0 m or 2.5 x 1.6 m (2,500 plants/ha) and 1.0 x 2.0 m (2,778 plants/ha, according to the agenda).
fichas.fertilizacion: Based on soil and plant analysis. Suggested: 200-100-160 of N-P-K, split 25-50-25 % from 15 days after transplanting to flowering, 50-50-50 % from flowering to start of harvest and 25-0-25 % from start of harvest to the first year, applying every 7 days. It is very demanding in boron, zinc and magnesium (correct with foliar sprays).
fichas.riego: Very demanding: shallow roots, the soil must be kept moist. Calculate water per plant according to evaporation and age; frequency according to variety, irrigation system, soil and climate.
enfermedades: Rots caused by Phytophthora, Pythium and Sclerotium
fichas.malezas: Start management from soil preparation and hand weed in the early stages; if needed, contact herbicides.
fichas.cosecha: From 7 to 18 months after transplanting depending on the variety, and up to 24 months with good plant health. Harvest according to the color stripes on the fruit: the farther the market, the fewer stripes. Potential of more than 100 t/ha with more than 2,000 plants/ha.
cuidados: Transplant from March to May to reduce virus-transmitting insects.
Plant more than 2,500 plants/ha so that plants with virus can be removed without losing stand.
Use genotypes tolerant to ringspot virus and control the insect vectors.
Form raised beds and drainage furrows to avoid root rots.
Monitor pests and exhaust other alternatives before chemical control.
Carry out sucker removal, leaf removal, sexing, fruit thinning and staking.
fichas.nota: Cycle null: the header says annual, but harvest lasts from 7 to 24 months. Table 34: gross income 320,000 = 80,000 kg × 4 $/kg and cost of 1.74 $/kg are consistent; the printed net income (320,000) equals gross income and does not add up (it should be 180,600), so it is null.

fichas.region: Semi-warm humid climate with summer rains, 850–2,000 m a.s.l. (Los Reyes, Peribán, Tocumbo, Tacámbaro, Ario, Taretan, Uruapan), with 50–250 chill hours; deep, well-drained, salt-free soils with organic matter, pH 5.8–7.2. It is produced mainly under irrigation; rainfed it needs at least 300 mm during the cycle.

siembra.texto: Subsoil, incorporate 5–8 t of compost with the harrow, furrow at 2 m or make beds 75 cm wide and 30 cm high, and mulch with plastic before transplanting. Then install trellises with 3 or 4 wires. The agenda does not give a planting date.

fichas.densidad: 50–60 cm between plants and 2.20 m between alleys: 8,000 to 14,000 plants per ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: The agenda only says to incorporate 5–8 t of compost during land preparation; it does not give a fertilization formula.
fichas.riego: Keep the soil at field capacity, generally with an irrigation depth of 25 mm per week; demand is higher in the hot, dry months.
fichas.malezas: With mulch, weeds are minimal: only periodic hand weeding in uncovered areas. Without mulch, mechanical control with a güiro (hand scraper), brush cutter or mower as often as necessary.
fichas.cosecha: Peak production is from December to March. Harvest only ripe and healthy fruit, early in the morning, carefully and without mixing varieties; protect it from the sun and take it promptly to pre-cooling. Store at 0 °C and 90–95 % relative humidity. Expected yield: 7.1 to 10 t/ha.
cuidados: Place vinegar traps to detect spotted wing drosophila in time and decide on control according to captures.
Control thrips before the flowers open.
Use quality, pathogen-free plants and biological products (Trichoderma, Bacillus) against Fusarium wilt.
Mulch the soil: it reduces weeds, compaction and loss of water and nutrients.
Train the plant on the trellises as it grows.
Maintain the cold chain from harvest: the fruit has a very short shelf life.
